overview.title: The walls that made the nickname
overview.p1: Taroudant’s ramparts stretch in ochre mud brick around the medina. They are the reason travellers call the town the Little Marrakech of the Souss — a fortified outline without the crowds of the imperial cities.
overview.p2: Walk outside the walls for the classic views, stop at the main gates, and catch late light when the brick glows. Pick segments rather than forcing a full loop in the heat.

moods.title: Ramparts through the day
moods.subtitle: Shade is limited — light and temperature decide how far you walk.

1.title: Cooler circuit
1.desc: Morning is kinder for longer stretches along the outside of the walls.

2.title: Harsh exposure
2.desc: Midday is punishing on open ground; keep walks short.

3.title: Golden ochre
3.desc: Late light is the classic Taroudant photo moment on the brick.

food.title: Eat near the walls
food.p1: No restaurants on the ramparts themselves. Return to the medina or Assarag for cafés and tagines.
food.p2: Bring water; treat food as a town-centre plan.
food.li2: Cafés near the main gates and Assarag.
food.li5: Do not rely on stalls along the walls.

1.title: How far to walk
1.desc: The full circuit is long. Choose a scenic segment and a gate rather than the entire loop.

2.title: Footwear
2.desc: Dusty and uneven ground outside the walls — closed shoes help.

3.title: Sunset
3.desc: Arrive before sunset for the best colour on the ochre brick.

q1.question: Can I walk on top of the walls?
q1.answer: Access varies by section; most visitors walk along the outside for views.

q2.question: How long is the full circuit?
q2.answer: Several kilometres — plan segments, not a forced full loop in summer heat.

q3.question: Best gate to start?
q3.answer: Ask your hotel for the nearest well-kept stretch and main bab.

q4.question: Family friendly?
q4.answer: Yes for short stretches with shade breaks in town.

q5.question: Need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required for an outer walk; useful for history of the gates.
